breaking: ASIA-PACIFIC: North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles towards the sea off its eastern coast, South Korea's military reports.
MIDDLE EAST: Attacks affecting Saudi Arabia and regional transport infrastructure heighten concerns over security and energy supplies.
ENERGY: Brent crude falls around 1.6% to $103.01 a barrel in early Monday trading, according to Reuters.
GLOBAL MARKETS: Investors assess geopolitical risks, rising borrowing costs and the approaching US corporate earnings season.
UKRAINE: A proposed energy-infrastructure ceasefire remains a diplomatic issue, with the details and implementation still developing.
TECHNOLOGY: Demand for artificial intelligence chips remains an important driver of expectations for major technology companies.

featured.title: North Korea's Missile Launches Raise Regional Security Concerns
featured.content: South Korea's military says North Korea launched multiple ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area towards the East Sea on Monday. One type reportedly travelled more than 900 kilometres. Japan also detected suspected ballistic missiles, with officials reporting that the projectiles had fallen into the sea. South Korea condemned the launches as violations of UN Security Council resolutions. The launches follow South Korea's recent test of a domestically developed hypersonic weapon. The circumstances and technical details of the latest North Korean launches remain under assessment.
featured.imageQuery: North Korea missile launch East Sea South Korea military October 2026

articles.title: North Korea Launches Multiple Ballistic Missiles
articles.content: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff reported that North Korea launched several ballistic missiles from near Pyongyang towards the East Sea on Monday morning. One type reportedly travelled more than 900 kilometres. Japan separately detected suspected ballistic missiles and said the projectiles had fallen into the sea. South Korea condemned the launches and called for them to stop. The incident follows Seoul's recent hypersonic weapon test and comes amid rising tensions between the two Koreas. The precise characteristics of all the missiles remain under investigation.
articles.imageQuery: North Korea ballistic missile launch military footage

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Faces Renewed Security Concerns After Reported Attacks
articles.content: Saudi Arabia has faced reported missile attacks affecting Riyadh's airport and other regional infrastructure over the weekend. Reporting from The Guardian's live coverage said the attacks killed 12 people and injured more than 300, while the Houthis claimed responsibility for strikes. The developments have intensified concerns about civilian safety, aviation and regional energy infrastructure. Details of individual incidents and responsibility should be followed through official statements and independently verified reporting as the situation develops.
articles.imageQuery: Riyadh Saudi Arabia international airport terminal

articles.title: Diplomatic Efforts Continue Amid Middle East Conflict
articles.content: The conflict involving Iran and wider regional tensions continue to shape international diplomacy. Questions surrounding maritime security, shipping routes and the Strait of Hormuz remain central to the global response. Any sustained interruption to commercial shipping could affect the movement of oil and liquefied natural gas, increasing uncertainty for importers and energy-dependent industries. Diplomatic statements and proposed arrangements should not be treated as a confirmed settlement until the relevant parties announce and implement an agreement.
articles.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz commercial oil tankers aerial view

articles.title: Oil Prices Ease as Investors Assess Supply Risks
articles.content: Brent crude futures fell approximately 1.6% to $103.01 a barrel in early Monday trading, while US crude futures also declined, according to Reuters. Prices have been moving in response to geopolitical developments and uncertainty over potential changes in energy exports. The market is also monitoring a proposal concerning energy supplies linked to the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Prices can change quickly, and the reported levels represent a market snapshot rather than a fixed price for the day.
articles.imageQuery: crude oil barrels refinery energy market

articles.title: European Governments Monitor Energy Costs and Supply Security
articles.content: European policymakers continue to face pressure to balance affordable energy, industrial competitiveness and reliable supplies. International conflicts and uncertainty surrounding refined petroleum products can influence transport, manufacturing and household bills. Governments and businesses are monitoring fuel availability, import costs and alternative supply routes. The extent of any additional price increases will depend on market conditions, shipping security and developments in international diplomacy.
articles.imageQuery: European energy infrastructure gas pipelines refinery

articles.title: Ukraine Energy Ceasefire Proposal Remains Under Discussion
articles.content: A proposal for an energy-focused ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine has become part of wider diplomatic discussions. Any arrangement would need clear terms, agreement from the parties and a way to monitor compliance. Energy infrastructure has remained a significant feature of the conflict, with attacks threatening electricity generation, fuel supplies and essential services. Until the terms are formally agreed and implemented, a comprehensive energy truce should not be presented as established.

articles.title: US Markets Prepare for Corporate Earnings and Inflation Data
articles.content: US investors are entering a closely watched period as major companies prepare to report earnings and fresh inflation data approaches. Markets are weighing expectations for corporate profits against borrowing costs, geopolitical uncertainty and the financial demands of investment in artificial intelligence. Technology companies remain an important influence on market performance, although results and price movements can vary considerably between businesses. Investors are also monitoring Treasury yields and signals about the future direction of monetary policy.
articles.imageQuery: New York Wall Street stock market financial district

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Chips Remain Central to Technology Market Expectations
articles.content: Demand for advanced chips used in artificial intelligence continues to influence expectations for the technology industry. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, a major producer of advanced semiconductors, is expected to report results this week. Investors will be watching for information about orders, manufacturing capacity and demand from technology companies. Strong interest in AI infrastructure is also prompting questions about investment costs, financing and how sustainable future spending will be.
articles.imageQuery: advanced semiconductor wafer artificial intelligence computer chips

articles.title: Asian Markets Trade Unevenly as Investors Assess Risks
articles.content: Asian share markets began the week unevenly as investors considered geopolitical developments, energy prices and the approaching corporate earnings season. Reuters reported declines in South Korean and Taiwanese shares, while mainland Chinese blue-chip stocks recorded a modest gain in early trading. Japanese markets were closed on Monday, and trading conditions were affected by a partial US market holiday. Movements may change as further company results and economic information become available.
articles.imageQuery: Asian financial district stock exchange market screens

articles.title: African Economies Remain Exposed to Energy and Shipping Costs
articles.content: African economies continue to monitor international oil prices, freight costs and the availability of essential imports. Higher fuel and transport expenses can place pressure on food distribution, agriculture, manufacturing and household purchasing power. Countries that depend on imported refined petroleum products may face particular challenges when global supplies tighten. Expanding local processing and diversifying supply routes can improve resilience, although domestic production does not automatically insulate consumers from international price movements.
articles.imageQuery: African port cargo ships fuel transport logistics

articles.title: Nigeria's Dangote Refinery Draws International Energy Attention
articles.content: Nigeria's Dangote Refinery remains an important development in the country's energy sector as global fuel supply disruptions create opportunities for refined petroleum exports. Reuters previously reported that the refinery had become an important supplier to European fuel markets during supply disruptions. The planned public share offering has also attracted attention from Nigerian investors. The wider significance includes domestic fuel availability, export earnings and capital-market participation. However, refinery output and an IPO do not guarantee lower retail fuel prices or investment returns.
articles.imageQuery: Dangote Petroleum Refinery Lekki Nigeria aerial view

articles.title: Investors Watch Bond Yields and the US Dollar
articles.content: Global financial markets are responding to changes in government bond yields, currency movements and expectations for interest rates. Higher long-term yields can increase borrowing costs for governments, companies and households, while affecting how investors value shares and other assets. Reuters reported that the US dollar remained firm as investors assessed the interest-rate outlook. The implications will depend on incoming economic data, central-bank decisions and developments in energy markets.
